conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
conflicts.issue: County Manager's $13M Recommendation vs. DPS's $27.735M Ask and Line-Item Expectations
conflicts.summary: Commissioners and county staff faced severe revenue constraints and modeled their $13M DPS allocation around state raises, the superintendent's teacher supplement, and Master's pay while suggesting a two-year phase-in for the $8.8M classified compensation study; DPS officials objected to line-item earmarking and urged immediate full funding for classified staff.
conflicts.side_a_position: Budget $13M within county revenue constraints, consider phasing the classified compensation study over two years, and expect stronger DPS communication after the December salary crisis.
side_a_arguments: Sales tax growth fell from $21M to $3.3M, forcing the county to freeze positions, cut department budgets, and propose a 3.25-cent property tax hike where $13M of $17.3M raised goes to DPS.

The $13M recommendation was intended to cover state mandates, the initial teacher supplement, Master's pay (promised at the October retreat), and charter pass-through, and the county previously phased its own pay study over two years.
conflicts.side_b_position: Protect DPS Board block-funding autonomy without county line-item conditions and prioritize fully funding the $8.8M classified compensation study immediately.
side_b_arguments: Interim Superintendent Kathy Moore stated it is inappropriate for county officials to publicly signal which DPS budget line items are funded, as the elected school board sets priorities.

Jovonia Lewis, Alexandra Valladares, and Natalie Beyer argued classified staff already lost a year after the reset ('our house is on fire') and cannot wait three years to reach market/living wages matching county employees (~$19/hour vs. $17/hour).
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote; both boards committed to ongoing monthly collaboration ahead of the county's May 28 public hearing and June 10 budget adoption.

conflicts.issue: Legal Authority for a School Adequate Public Facility Ordinance (SAPFO) vs. Advisory Task Force
conflicts.summary: During discussion of DPS's projected 4,800-student growth from approved developments, commissioners and BOE members expressed interest in pursuing an Orange County-style SAPFO or growth controls, while County Attorney Curtis Massey cautioned against assuming the County has legal authority to enact one.
conflicts.side_a_position: Explore an intergovernmental Growth & Education Task Force alongside studying Orange County's SAPFO and UDO revisions to manage school overcrowding.
side_a_arguments: Each newly approved development creates unfunded school seat costs ($100,000 per seat) that fall on county taxpayers without developer concurrency.
Consulting Orange County officials could clarify how their SAPFO and task force operate to see what tools Durham can adapt.
conflicts.side_b_position: Caution that Durham County's prior adequate public facility ordinance was struck down as exceeding county authority and that Orange County relies on a special local act.
side_b_arguments: Under the 2006 Durham Landowners precedent, North Carolina counties lack general statutory authority to impose education impact fees or concurrency denials without state enabling legislation.
Any enforceable growth coordination also requires City Council participation since municipal rezonings drive residential approvals.
conflicts.resolution: County Attorney Curtis Massey agreed to consult Orange County Attorney John Roberts on how Orange County's SAPFO was authorized, while commissioners directed Deborah Craig-Ray to consider adding developer school impact fee authority to the state legislative agenda.

conflicts.issue: Codifying Pre-K Expansion Funding Commitments in the BOE–BOCC MOU
conflicts.summary: BOE Chair Rogers suggested revising the BOE–BOCC Memorandum of Understanding to lock in multi-year Pre-K expansion targets and timelines, prompting differing perspectives among commissioners.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support revisiting the BOE–BOCC MOU to ensure alignment and institutionalize support for Pre-K expansion and the new data-sharing MOA.
side_a_arguments: Board compositions change over time, and an updated MOU can ensure the data-sharing agreement and long-term Pre-K priorities remain consistent.
Shared alignment strengthens joint advocacy to the state and business community.
conflicts.side_b_position: Caution that codifying funding figures in an MOU could inadvertently cap or reduce commissioners' otherwise aggressive annual Pre-K investments.
side_b_arguments: Commissioners have repeatedly pushed staff to invest more in Pre-K each year—reaching roughly $8–10 million—without needing a contractual floor.
An MOU has different perceived weight across boards and may not be necessary to sustain funding.
conflicts.resolution: No formal action taken; commissioners agreed to stay engaged on the Pre-K data-sharing MOA and future MOU discussions.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Interpretation of Public School Forum Funding Effort Rankings
conflicts.summary: Natalie Beyer cited Public School Forum rankings showing Durham 8th in ability to pay but 42nd in relative funding effort to urge greater local investment, while Commissioner Wendy Jacobs rejected the ranking as omitting $62M in direct county education spending.
conflicts.side_a_position: Durham County has capacity to stretch further on K-12 operating support given its 8th-place ability-to-pay rank versus 42nd-place effort rank.
side_a_arguments: Public School Forum's local finance study ranks Durham 8th in ability to pay but 42nd in relative funding effort.
DPS's lowest-paid staff remain at $17/hour compared to over $19/hour for county employees.
conflicts.side_b_position: The Public School Forum effort metric omits major county-funded school expenditures and understates Durham's high per-pupil commitment.
side_b_arguments: The study excludes $62 million in direct county allocations such as school debt service and Pre-K.
Under the manager's proposed budget, Durham ranks 3rd highest statewide in per-pupil funding ($5,030 per pupil) despite ranking 22nd in per-capita assessed valuation.
conflicts.resolution: Debated without formal action; Commissioner Heidi Carter also noted aspiring to rank 1st in funding while balancing taxpayer burdens.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and the Durham County Board of County Commissioners held their Joint Quarterly Meeting on November 13, 2024, presided over by Chair Millicent Rogers, welcoming newly appointed County Manager Claudia Hager and new DPS Chief Operating Officer Dr. Larry Webb and Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Teeter. Both boards unanimously approved the agenda, amended and approved the August 6, 2024 joint minutes to clarify superintendent titles, and adopted an amended 2025 joint meeting calendar moving the November 2025 session to November 12 to avoid a state school board conference conflict. Operational Services staff presented a comprehensive update on universal Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) school meals, student-driven menus, and $13 million in deferred school nutrition kitchen infrastructure needs alongside $1.6 million earmarked in FY 2024-25 operational capital outlay. Commissioners and board members also reviewed enrollment forecasts, Dr. Anthony Lewis's first four months as superintendent, staff compensation implementation, Alliance mental health funding, and teacher housing before closing without public comment as county commissioners neared loss of quorum.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Welcome to County Manager Claudia Hager, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The joint quarterly session of the BOCC and DPS Board of Education was called to order, and Board members welcomed newly appointed County Manager Claudia Hager. Commissioner Jacobs moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Approval of August 6, 2024 Joint Meeting Minutes and Capital Planning Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members discussed follow-up items from the August 6 minutes, including a pending Durham Pre-K agreement update and coordination with city and county planning departments on adequate school facilities and growth tracking ahead of a February capital planning update. An amendment was approved to clarify Dr. Anthony Lewis as incoming superintendent and Kathy Moore as interim superintendent in the August 6 minutes before approving the minutes as amended.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Amendment and amended minutes passed unanimously

agenda_items.title: Introduction of DPS Chief Operating Officer Dr. Larry Webb and Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Teeter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Anthony Lewis introduced two key cabinet hires: Dr. Larry Webb as Chief Operating Officer effective November 18 (joining from Franklin County) and Jeremy Teeter, MBA, as Chief Financial Officer effective November 4.

agenda_items.title: Approval of 2025 BOCC/BOE Joint Meeting Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board member Jessica Carda-Auten flagged a conflict between the proposed November 18, 2025 joint meeting date and the North Carolina School Boards Association conference. Members agreed to shift the November 2025 joint meeting to Wednesday, November 12 and approved the calendar as amended.

agenda_items.title: Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) Meal Participation Update and Kitchen Infrastructure Needs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matthew Palmer and nutrition leadership reported on student-led scratch cooking and DPS becoming the largest North Carolina district to implement universal CEP free breakfast and lunch effective July 1, budgeting conservatively for a 14% lunch participation increase. Officials detailed $13 million in deferred kitchen infrastructure needs and $1.6 million earmarked in FY 2024-25 operational capital outlay, while commissioners questioned whether to pursue a public-private partnership central kitchen feasibility study versus prioritizing repairs to existing school kitchens.

agenda_items.title: District Enrollment Forecast, Superintendent Entry Update, Budget Implementation, and Mental Health
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff shared Pre-K through high school enrollment growth and capacity forecasts, and Dr. Lewis reflected on entering his fourth month as superintendent. Commissioners and board members requested follow-up reporting on FY 2024-25 certified, classified, and Master's pay budget implementation, discussed Alliance mental health funding and teacher housing, and deferred the Durham Pre-K MOA until staff prepares materials for a future joint meeting.

votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE voice vote; individual BOE roll call not taken.
votes.discussion_detail: Following welcoming remarks for County Manager Claudia Hager, Commissioner Jacobs moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the November 13, 2024 joint quarterly meeting agenda. No objections were raised and the voice vote carried unanimously.

votes.item_title: Amend August 6, 2024 Minutes to Clarify Superintendent Titles
votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE voice vote; individual BOE roll call not taken.
votes.discussion_detail: During discussion of the August 6, 2024 joint meeting minutes, a board member requested clarifying edits to distinguish Dr. Anthony Lewis as incoming superintendent and Kathy Moore as interim superintendent for historical clarity. Commissioner Jacobs moved the revision and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded; the amendment passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve August 6, 2024 Joint Meeting Minutes as Amended
votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE voice vote; original main motion moved at 00:13:48 by Joy Harrell-Goff and seconded by Commissioner Jacobs.
votes.discussion_detail: After adopting the title-clarification amendment and discussing upcoming February capital planning updates with county and city planning staff, the joint bodies voted unanimously by voice vote to approve the August 6, 2024 minutes as amended.

votes.item_title: Approve 2025 BOCC/BOE Joint Meeting Calendar as Amended (Moving November Meeting to Nov. 12)
votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE voice vote; individual BOE roll call not taken.
votes.discussion_detail: Following an initial motion by Commissioner Jacobs seconded by Natalie Beyer to approve the 2025 joint meeting calendar, Jessica Carda-Auten identified a conflict between November 18, 2025 and the state school board association conference. Commissioner Jacobs moved to amend the calendar to move the November 2025 meeting to Wednesday, November 12, seconded by Emily Chávez (with Natalie Beyer concurring), and the amended calendar passed unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: BOCC BOE joint meeting August 6, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 6, 2024 joint meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners and Durham Public Schools Board of Education, DPS planners projected 4,800 additional students from 220 city-approved developments—including a 38% surge in the Eastern region—prompting calls for an intergovernmental Growth & Education Task Force and exploration of school impact fees or an Adequate Public Facility Ordinance. Leaders also reviewed plans to expand Pre-K from 81 to 103 classrooms across all 32 elementary schools, discussed a FERPA-compliant Teaching Strategies GOLD data-sharing MOU and potential updates to the BOE-BOCC MOU, and unanimously approved prior joint meeting minutes. Interim Superintendent Moore presented DPS's $27.3 million local budget infusion, teacher supplements, classified salary schedules (3%–17% increases), $25–30 million in deferred capital needs, and an 85% departmental budget release amid County warnings of constrained future revenues, before hearing public comment from Durham for DSA challenging DPS's Durham School of the Arts relocation study.

agenda_items.title: Student Enrollment Forecast, School Capacity, and Growth Management ('Synchronizing')
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS school planner Matthew Palmer (with demographic planner Vitaly Ratsky and Planning Director Sara Young) reported 31,000 students across 35,000 seats (89% utilization) and projected 4,800 additional students from 220 city-approved residential developments—including a 38% surge in the Eastern region where Neal Middle School is already at capacity—at a construction cost of $100,000 per seat. Noting North Carolina prohibits education impact fees (under the 2006 Durham Landowners ruling) and Durham lacks a School Adequate Public Facility Ordinance (SAPFO) like Orange County, Palmer proposed an intergovernmental Growth & Education Task Force. Commissioners Allam, Jacobs, Carter, and Burns discussed presenting to City Council, adding developer school impact fees to the NCACC legislative agenda, studying Orange County's SAPFO and UDO concurrency tools, safe routes to school, and land-banking/surplus school sites, while County Attorney Curtis Massey cautioned that Orange County's SAPFO relies on a special local act.

agenda_items.title: Expanding Access to Early Education (Pre-K) and Data-Sharing MOU Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pittman and DPS staff presented a plan to expand Pre-K from 30 of 32 elementary schools (81 classrooms, up to 1,137 seats) in 2024–25 to all 32 schools (103 classrooms, nearly 1,500 seats), outlining cost estimates of up to $980,000 in one-time facility retrofits for unlicensed sites, ~$240,000+ in annual classroom operating costs plus wraparound care and busing, and multilingual needs for the 22% non-English-speaking family population. Durham Pre-K Director Dr. Linda Chappelle reported 42% coverage of Durham's 4-year-olds toward the 75% universal goal and detailed a FERPA-compliant Teaching Strategies GOLD data-sharing MOU across DPS, Head Start, NC Pre-K, and Durham Pre-K. BOE Chair Rogers and Commissioners Carter and Jacobs discussed whether and how to update the joint BOE–BOCC MOU around Pre-K expansion and data sharing.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Joint BOCC–BOE Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With quorum confirmed after the Pre-K presentation, Chair Nida Allam entertained a motion to approve the prior joint meeting minutes. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved approval and BOE Chair Rogers seconded, passing unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: DPS FY 2024-25 Budget, Salary Schedules, and Capital Needs Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Superintendent Moore detailed DPS's $27.3 million local funding infusion ($20 million general fund increase, $6 million ARPA, $716,000 Pre-K, plus $2 million additional capital), certified teacher pay changes (1.55%–7.05% state raise plus $800 local supplement, 10% master's pay, and $200–$300/month EC/ELL supplements), and classified salary schedules providing 3% to 17% increases above final FY24 levels (effective September with October retroactive pay for July–August). Moore noted DPS released only 85% of local department budgets to save ~$6 million and rebuild fund balance amid $25–30 million in deferred HVAC, fire-safety, and CEP cafeteria needs. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs warned the County faces 'uncharted territory' financially and cannot sustain this year's funding jump, while Commissioner Heidi Carter raised concern that DPS's lowest-paid staff (<$18/hour) lag the County's $19.79/hour living wage and worried about reallocating 2022 bond funds.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment: Durham for DSA Criticism of DSA Relocation Closure Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: John Hodges-Copple, representing Durham for DSA, criticized DPS consultants' Durham School of the Arts closure study and the prior week's public hearing as unadvertised, rushed, and lacking a valid statutory cost comparison for renovating the current DSA campus or evaluating the community option. He warned both boards that unprecedented borrowing for a relocated DSA at high interest rates would crowd out elementary school projects, County CIP priorities, and future operating budgets.

votes.item_title: Approval of Joint BOCC–BOE Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Joint BOCC–BOE vote; Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton was not recorded speaking in this transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Confirming quorum, Chair Nida Allam called for a motion to approve the joint meeting minutes. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved approval and BOE Chair Rogers seconded; both boards approved the minutes unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham Board of County Commissioners held a joint quarterly meeting on May 14, 2024, presided over in-person by Vice Chair Emily Chávez (with Chair Bettina Umstead joining via Zoom), featuring presentations on Durham Pre-K, the DPS FY 2024-25 $27.735 million budget request, the County Manager's $13 million recommended DPS increase, and myFutureNC educational attainment data. While no formal votes occurred, sharp disagreements emerged over the county's funding shortfall relative to DPS's $8.8 million classified compensation study, county expectations around which DPS line items the $13 million recommendation should cover, and whether Public School Forum effort rankings accurately reflect Durham County's $62 million in direct school capital and Pre-K spending. Interim Superintendent Kathy Moore pushed back on county officials signaling line-item preferences, while school board members urged commissioners not to delay classified staff pay for a third year.

agenda_items.title: Durham Pre-K Update and Long-Term Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following technical delays, Dr. Linda Chappelle presented on Durham Pre-K's goal of reaching 75% of four-year-olds (targeting 42% next year), expansion to 25 of 32 DPS elementary schools, sliding-scale fees above 400% of federal poverty, and North Carolina's largest Early Childhood Apprenticeship Program (~100 waitlisted). She urged DPS to develop a long-term Pre-K facilities/cost plan, revisit wrap-around care and transportation barriers, and recommit to cross-agency data sharing.

agenda_items.title: DPS FY 2024-25 Budget Proposal and Internal Fiscal Measures
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Superintendent Kathy Moore presented the Board of Education's $27.735 million local funding request—including $6.578M in legislative mandates, $3.1M for teacher supplements, $1.39M for EC/ESL/self-contained supplements, ~$1.3M for Master's pay, $8.8M to implement the revised classified compensation study, $4.253M charter school pass-through, $716K for 45 Murray-Massenburg Pre-K seats, and $1.5M maintenance—alongside deferred needs ($8M tech refresh, $25–$30M HVAC/lifecycle, $10M fire safety, CEP cafeteria equipment) and internal austerity cuts. Commissioners asked whether the classified study could be phased over two years and noted the county's proposed $13M increase did not match the full $27.735M ask.

agenda_items.title: County Manager's Recommended FY 2024-25 Budget Implications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Joanne Sowell and Deputy County Manager Dr. Claudia Hager summarized the manager's recommended FY 2024-25 county budget, citing slowing sales tax growth ($21M down to $3.3M), a $50M+ request gap, a recommended 3.25-cent property tax increase ($17.3M), and $13M in new DPS current expense funding ($5,030 per pupil) plus ~$947K–$950K for Pre-K. Tense exchanges followed over Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns's frustration with post-December DPS communication, Hager's note that the $13M modeled Master's pay and teacher supplements rather than the classified study, Moore's objection to county line-item signaling, and disputes over Public School Forum funding effort rankings.

agenda_items.title: myFutureNC Durham Educational Attainment Update and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: North Central Regional Impact Manager Brett Brenton presented Durham County's educational attainment profile, noting Durham has already exceeded its 75% attainment goal for 25–44-year-olds while facing a 27.9% remaining gap, 9.7% opportunity youth rate, 55% living-wage rate ($49,531 MIT benchmark), and top growth priorities in NC Pre-K, math performance, and chronic absenteeism. Board members and commissioners discussed FAFSA completion, dropout-age legislation, apprenticeships, and North Carolina's three-year graduation law before adjourning at 02:30:34 with no public comments.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2024-03-14 9:00 AM - Joint Board of County Commissioners and Board of Education Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 14, 2024 Joint Board of County Commissioners and Durham Public Schools Board of Education meeting—initially presided over by DPS Chair Bettina Umstead before DPS Vice Chair Emily Chávez assumed the chair at 02:13:12—the boards approved the agenda unanimously by voice vote (moved by BOCC Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns and seconded by DPS Board Member Millicent Rogers) with no split or contested votes occurring. DPS staff (Mr. Johnson and Frederick Davis II) delivered a capital planning update highlighting 30–40% post-COVID construction inflation, $513 million in combined 2022 and prior unspent bond capacity, $14 million spent over three years on indoor air quality and safe pathways, $10 million in limited obligation funds for chillers, boilers, and fire alarms, and plans to use Northern High School as swing space to cut occupied elementary school renovation timelines from three years to 18 months. Following a county financial update citing a 36% fund balance reserve policy, commissioners and board members discussed tight FY budget constraints (~$182 million in county operating funding for DPS), state underfunding, local funding flowing to 47 charter schools and private school vouchers, low-wage worker compensation, and an 11% DPS pay increase supported by $4 million in county funds. The meeting concluded with a staff presentation on expanding the federal Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) for universal free school meals to serve roughly 30,000 children daily, public comments from Durham CAN and Poverty Action Team advocates urging DPS to submit the CEP application, and closing remarks prioritizing Pre-K and requesting county materials eight hours in advance for future joint meetings.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, November 17 Minutes Review, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Joint County Commission and School Board meeting was called to order with a quorum from both bodies. During review of the November 17 meeting minutes, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs noted that public comment entries only stated that 11 people spoke and requested that future minutes include speakers' names and general topics in accordance with county practice. BOCC Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns then moved to approve the agenda as presented before acting on the minutes, seconded by DPS Board Member Millicent Rogers, and the motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Capital Planning Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS capital staff Mr. Johnson and Frederick Davis II briefed both boards on capital renewal and improvements across 56 sites totaling 6 million square feet (average building age roughly 25 years), citing $6 million in annual county capital funding, $10 million in limited obligation funds for chillers, boilers, and fire alarm systems, and $14 million spent over three years on indoor air quality and safe pathways. Presenters explained that 30–40% post-COVID construction inflation required reprioritizing the 10-year plan across $513 million in combined 2022 bond and $90 million prior unspent bond dollars, alongside a 2024 facility conditions assessment and construction progress at Murray-Massenburg. Board members asked about slide readability, the online bond-spending dashboard tracker, MWBE goals, $10 million in fire marshal projects over five years against a $6 million budget, and using Northern High School as swing space to shorten occupied elementary school renovations from three years to 18 months.

agenda_items.title: Fund Balance Reserves, Joint FY Budget Priorities, and Employee Compensation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Closing a financial presentation after a truncated portion of the transcript, staff noted the undesignated fund balance reserve maintained for emergencies in alignment with the 36% overall fund balance policy, and the boards confirmed keeping the agenda without a staff presentation or the Pre-K memo. After DPS Vice Chair Emily Chávez took over chairing at 02:13:12, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs warned that local taxpayers are increasingly covering state responsibilities across nearly $182 million in DPS operating costs, 47 charter schools, and private school vouchers, while urging attention to lowest-wage workers given roughly 25% of Durham residents work for Duke. Commissioner Heidi Carter emphasized balancing a constricted budget against DPS's real needs and recalled working with Durham CAN on a living wage policy in 2004, while DPS Board Member Millicent Rogers urged joint Raleigh advocacy over charter school student returns after the 20-day ADM count and highlighted an 11% DPS pay raise enabled by $4 million in county funding.

agenda_items.title: Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) Free School Meals Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters shared research-based information on the federal Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) for universal free school meals, explaining how CEP removes the family burden of free and reduced-price lunch applications and connects to Title I funding. They noted that applying and being accepted this year would allow DPS to participate for at least three years and provide nutritious meals to approximately 30,000 children every day. Acting chair Emily Chávez thanked presenters and advocates, noted the meeting was over time, and stated that the DPS Board of Education would hold a follow-up discussion as a board the next week.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Universal Free Meals and Closing Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Six public speakers addressed the boards for one minute each, including Reverend James Blake (Fisher Memorial United Holy Church and Durham CAN), Kyla Perry, Norma Ortiz, Latasha Williams (Southern Durham High School parent and Durham County Poverty Action Team), and a former third- and fourth-grade teacher. Advocates noted that 28 of 56 DPS schools participate in CEP and urged the board to sign the CEP application to provide universal free meals across all schools to combat food insecurity and improve classroom behavior. In closing at 03:00:35, acting chair Emily Chávez reiterated that the boards will prioritize Pre-K and ask the county to provide materials eight hours in advance next time before adjourning at 03:00:55.

votes.notes: Voice vote approved unanimously ('all in favor say aye. Any opposed? Agenda has approved unanimously'); individual roll-call votes and exact count of members present were not recorded in the transcript digest. Mover appears in ASR as 'Vice Chair Bern' (Nimasheena Burns) and seconder as 'Council Board Member, Bill and Senator Rogers' (Millicent Rogers).
votes.discussion_detail: Following review of the November 17 meeting minutes and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs's request to include speaker names and topics in future minutes, BOCC Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns noted the boards needed to formally approve the agenda first and moved to approve the agenda as is.
